title: request-correlator-microtag-timeline-stitching
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: When requests are coalesced into batches and kernel launches are interleaved, it is challenging to map individual GPU kernels back to the originating request shard and logical phase (e.g., tokenization, kv-lookup, attention, decode-step). Current NVTX ranges and trace spans are either too coarse or too noisy for deterministic per-request cost attribution.

Proposal: Implement a lightweight request-correlator that stamps each request shard with a compact 64-bit microtag propagated through the runtime work item. NVTX ranges and trace spans will include the microtag + a short phase marker so post-processing can stitch a microtimeline per request. The pipeline will fuse scheduler launch logs, NVTX envelopes, and per-kernel counters to produce per-request per-kernel metrics (time, SM utilization, memory ops) with sampling to bound overhead.

Goals: (1) enable precise per-request kernel attribution for perf regression and cost analysis, (2) keep runtime overhead <0.5% on tail latency for sampled traces and throughput impact <3% at 1% sampling, (3) produce a compact telemetry envelope suitable for downstream analytics and dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime can attach and propagate a 64-bit microtag to all work items and NVTX ranges for sampled requests
Post-process pipeline reconstructs a per-request microtimeline for sampled traces with >95% mapping accuracy (matching scheduler logs)
End-to-end sampled overhead measured and documented: latency p50/p95/p99 delta and throughput impact under 1% sampling
Grafana dashboard showing per-kernel time attribution across phases and a new per-request cost card
Ship feature behind a runtime flag and sampling config; rollout plan documented in the runbook
implementation_steps: Spike: add microtag field to WorkItem struct and propagate through scheduler (local branch) - 2d
Define NVTX naming envelope: "r=<microtag>:p=<phase>:k=<kernel_name>" and implement NVTX emitters around kernel launches - 3d
Add lightweight trace span enrichment for all runtime phases (tokenize, prefill, attention-kv, matmul, reduce, decode-step) - 2d
Sampling policy: implement probabilistic sampler at request ingress and ensure microtagging only for sampled requests; add opt-in config per deployment - 1d
Telemetry pipeline: extend collector to parse microtag NVTX envelopes, correlate with scheduler launch logs, and emit per-request per-kernel metrics - 5d
Dashboarding: add Grafana panels and a per-request cost card; wire to existing observability dashboards - 2d
Rollout: enable behind flag, run internal soak for 2 weeks on dedicated infra, iterate on naming and size limits - 7d
notes_and_updates: 2026-03-01 Ava Martinez: Created ticket after a spike showed repeated ambiguity mapping launch timestamps to request shards during high-concurrency workloads.
2026-03-03 Rohan Patel: RFC posted to Confluence (see link). Chosen microtag = 64-bit (randomized on ingress) to avoid registry; decided against global monotonic id to reduce contention.
2026-03-04 Nina Cho (perf): Reviewed approach — recommended keeping NVTX string under 128 bytes to avoid cuProfiler truncation; requested benchmark targets for sampler overhead.
2026-03-06 Marcus Lee (observability): Asked for a fallback strategy when kernel names are mangled by backend; agreed to emit both short kernel alias and full id where available.

2026-03-08 Rohan Patel: Implemented WorkItem microtag propagation and added NVTX emitters in a feature branch: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/1826. Initial unit tests added for propagation correctness.
2026-03-09 Performance run: 1% sampling on x8 A100 cluster; observed +0.18% median latency, +1.6% throughput delta under synthetic L=1024 load. Documented in perf-run-2026-03-09.md.

2026-03-11 Code review feedback (PR 1826): split NVTX envelope builder into util module; add defensive guard when WorkItem already has a microtag; update comments explaining sampling boundary conditions.

2026-03-12 Rohan Patel: Opened telemetry collector PR to parse microtag + phase markers and correlate to scheduler logs: github.com/redwood/telemetry/pull/443. Added integration test that replays scheduler logs against captured NVTX events.

Follow-ups: (a) discuss retention and PII review for persisted microtags with Security, (b) determine default sampling rate per environment, (c) add an opt-out cluster-level toggle for high-throughput Dedicated customers.
